sentences.text: If you remember only one rule from this whole course, make it this one.
Rule two says nothing in the rules excuses you from the consequences of neglecting ordinary seamanship.
In plain English: the rule book is not a shield.
You must pay attention to every danger and every special circumstance, including what the other boat can and can’t do.
And sometimes, to avoid immediate danger, you have to depart from the rules.
That isn’t just allowed, it’s expected.
Here’s how I think about it.
Picture yourself as the stand-on boat, holding your course, while a tug pushing a barge clearly isn’t turning.
If you hold your course right into that barge, you followed the rules, and you’ll still be found at fault.
Notice too that the rules almost never say right of way.
They say who keeps out of the way, and who stands on.
That’s a mindset, not a privilege.
